# CLI reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_cli_docs.py from `ag --help`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Exit codes (stable, safe for scripts and agents to rely on):

| code | meaning |
|-----:|---------|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | error (bad input, missing object, I/O, ...); message on stderr |
| 2 | usage error (unknown command or option) |
| 3 | **blocked**: something you can provide is missing (approval, validation, lease token) |
| 4 | **refused**: conflict, policy denial or invalid request; the stream was not changed |

Which commands use 3 and 4, and the commands that exit 1 on a problem they found, are listed in [Help topics](help-topics.md#exit-codes) (`ag help exit-codes`).

Global options: `-C/--repo`, `--as <identity>` (or `AG_IDENTITY`), `--json`, `--color <auto|always|never>`
(`NO_COLOR` is honoured; nothing is coloured in a pipe), `-q/--quiet`, `-v/--verbose`.
Concept pages are available in the terminal: `ag help workflow|policy|leases|identities|revisions|exit-codes|json|config`, and in [Help topics](help-topics.md). Machine-readable output: [`--json` shapes](cli-json.md). Environment and files: [Configuration](configuration.md). Shell completion and man pages: [Completions and man pages](completions.md).

## ag

```text
AgentGit: an agent-native source control system. People, agents and CI change one codebase at the same time; every change lands through a proposal, and a per-stream policy decides what must be true first (validation of the exact tree, approvals, leases, an autonomy envelope for agents).

Usage: ag [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init         Create a repository in the current directory
  migrate      Migrate every branch and tag from a full local Git clone or bundle into a new repository
  status       Summarize the workspace, your proposals, leases, task and remote at a glance
  snapshot     Record the working directory as a new snapshot
  sync         Bring the stream's latest head into the workspace
  log          Show history
  show         Show one changeset and what it changed
  diff         Show differences between two revisions, or the working directory and its snapshot
  cat          Print a file as of a revision: `ag cat main:src/lib.rs`
  blame        Show which changeset introduced each line of a file
  ls           List a directory as of a revision
  checkout     Write a revision's files into a new directory
  portability  List what a revision contains that Windows, macOS or Linux file systems cannot hold
  stream       Manage streams
  propose      Publish a snapshot and open a proposal to integrate it
  proposal     List, review, update or close proposals
  integrate    Integrate a proposal into its stream
  preview      Show what integrating a proposal would do, without doing it
  explain      Say why a proposal does not land yet, in plain words, with the exact commands that fix each reason
  op           Inspect or resume operations
  recover      Resume interrupted operations and expire stale ones
  queue        The ordered integration queue
  policy       Show or change stream policy
  validate     Run checks and issue signed attestations
  agent        Agent identities and runs
  task         Tasks and their dependencies
  lease        Soft and exclusive leases with fencing tokens
  provenance   Signed provenance of agent-made changes
  predict      Predict overlapping work
  workspace    Create, list and remove workspaces (isolated lines of work in their own directories)
  trace        Show the audit trail of an object, proposal, run or stream
  audit        Verify the tamper-evident audit chain
  verify       Check the integrity of the whole repository
  gc           Delete unreachable objects (safe: fails closed, honours a grace period)
  reindex      Rebuild derived indexes from the object store
  backup       Write a verified, consistent copy of the repository to a new directory
  git          Import from or export to Git (needs the `git` command)
  clone        Clone a repository from an `ag-server`
  fetch        Download new history from the server
  pull         Fetch, then fast-forward the local stream and bring the workspace up to date
  push         Upload your snapshot and open a proposal on the server
  remote       Manage remotes and work with proposals, events and policy on a server
  login        Save a server credential once; `clone`, `fetch`, `push` and `remote` then need no token plumbing
  auth         Inspect saved server connections without printing credentials
  logout       Forget a saved server credential
  pin          Pin a revision so garbage collection keeps it
  unpin        Remove a pin
  pins         List pins
  doctor       Check the installation, the repository, your identity and every remote's credential
  config       Show, get, set and locate configuration (the user file; the repository's settings are shown read-only)
  completions  Print a shell completion script: bash, zsh, fish, powershell or elvish
  man          Print the man page, or write one page per command with --dir
  version      Print the version, the protocol and the JSON schema version
  help         Show help for a command, or a topic: workflow, policy, leases, identities, revisions, exit-codes, json, config

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>
          Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)

      --as <IDENTITY>
          Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY

      --json
          Machine-readable JSON output

      --color <WHEN>
          Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never

  -q, --quiet
          Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown

  -v, --verbose
          Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Common workflow:
  ag init --namespace me/app     create a repository in this directory
  ag snapshot -m "message"       record the working directory
  ag propose -t "title"          publish it and open a proposal
  ag integrate PROPOSAL          land it (policy decides; any unique id prefix works)
  ag explain [PROPOSAL]          if it does not land: why, and the exact commands that fix it

Where am I, is it healthy:
  ag status                      workspace, your proposals, leases, task and remote at a glance
  ag doctor                      check the installation, the repository, your identity and every remote

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 blocked (provide what is missing and run it again),
4 refused (conflict, policy denial; the stream was not changed). Add --json for machine-readable output.

Help topics (ag help TOPIC): workflow, policy, leases, identities, revisions, exit-codes, json, config
Shell completion: ag completions bash|zsh|fish|powershell|elvish     Man pages: ag man --dir DIR
Documentation: https://github.com/Paffin/AgentGit/tree/main/docs
```

## ag init

```text
Create a repository in the current directory

Usage: ag init [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>             Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --namespace <NAMESPACE>  Repository namespace, e.g. `acme/webapp` (default: `local/<directory name>`)
      --as <IDENTITY>          Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --stream <STREAM>        Name of the first stream [default: main]
      --json                   Machine-readable JSON output
      --storage <FILE>         JSON file with the `storage` section (PostgreSQL metadata and/or S3 objects); see docs/operations/postgres-and-s3.md. Default: a SQLite file and local objects under `.ag/`
      --color <WHEN>           Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
      --preset <NAME>          Store a ready-made policy for the first stream: solo, team, agents or strict (`ag policy preset list`)
      --admin <IDENTITY>       Identity pattern allowed to change the policy (repeatable). Default: you
  -q, --quiet                  Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
      --issuer <IDENTITY=KEY>  Trust this CI issuer to sign the `tests` check: IDENTITY=PUBLIC_KEY, e.g. service:ci=<64 hex digits>
  -v, --verbose                Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
      --ci-key <NAME>          Trust the signing key NAME of this repository (created if missing; `ag validate keygen NAME` makes the same key): the issuer becomes service:NAME
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
```

## ag migrate

```text
Migrate every branch and tag from a full local Git clone or bundle into a new repository

Usage: ag migrate [OPTIONS] --namespace <NAMESPACE> <SOURCE> <DESTINATION>

Arguments:
  <SOURCE>       Full local Git clone, mirror or self-contained .bundle file
  <DESTINATION>  New destination directory. It must not exist

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>             Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --namespace <NAMESPACE>  Destination namespace, for example acme/webapp
      --as <IDENTITY>          Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --dry-run                Verify the migration and report limitations without publishing a repository
      --allow-lossy            Accept reported omissions, unresolved LFS pointers and unsupported refs
      --json                   Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>           Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet                  Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose                Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
```

## ag status

```text
Summarize the workspace, your proposals, leases, task and remote at a glance

Usage: ag status [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>             Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
  -w, --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Workspace name [default: default]
      --as <IDENTITY>          Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --dir <DIR>              Working directory of the workspace (required for non-default workspaces)
      --json                   Machine-readable JSON output
      --remote                 Also ask each remote's server for its current head (needs the network and a credential)
      --color <WHEN>           Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet                  Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose                Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
```

## ag diff

```text
Show differences between two revisions, or the working directory and its snapshot

Usage: ag diff [OPTIONS] [REVS]...

Arguments:
  [REVS]...  With two revisions: diff A to B. With one: diff it against its first parent. With none: diff the workspace head against the working directory

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>             Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
  -U, --context <CONTEXT>      Lines of context [default: 3]
      --as <IDENTITY>          Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
  -w, --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Workspace (for the no-argument form) [default: default]
      --dir <DIR>              Workspace directory (for the no-argument form)
      --json                   Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>           Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet                  Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose                Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
```

## ag blame

```text
Show which changeset introduced each line of a file

Usage: ag blame [OPTIONS] <SPEC>

Arguments:
  <SPEC>  `[REV:]PATH`, for example `src/lib.rs`, `main:src/lib.rs` or `@:README.md`. Without a revision, the workspace head (or the default stream) is used

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>                 Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
  -L, --lines <START,END>          Only these lines, `START,END` (1-based, inclusive)
      --as <IDENTITY>              Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --max-commits <MAX_COMMITS>  Visit at most this many changesets; older lines are marked as a boundary [default: 100000]
      --copies                     Follow files that were created as copies of another file: lines a copy took over are blamed on whoever wrote them in the source (identical content, or at least 50% of the bytes in common with a neighbouring or co-modified file)
      --json                       Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>               Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet                      Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose                    Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version
```

## ag stream

```text
Manage streams

Usage: ag stream [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list    List streams and their heads
  create  Create a stream, optionally at an existing published revision
  show    Show one stream
  reflog  Show the append-only history of head movements

Options:
```

## ag integrate

```text
Integrate a proposal into its stream

Usage: ag integrate [OPTIONS] <PROPOSAL>

Arguments:
  <PROPOSAL>  Proposal id

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>                      Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --key <KEY>                       Idempotency key (default: derived from the proposal; repeating resumes/replays). Not the issuer key of `ag validate run --key`; `--idempotency-key` is the unambiguous spelling [alias: --idempotency-key]
      --as <IDENTITY>                   Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --fencing-token <FENCING_TOKENS>  Fencing token(s) of exclusive leases the author holds
      --json                            Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>                    Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet                           Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose                         Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                            Print help
  -V, --version                         Print version

Exit codes: 0 integrated, 3 blocked (provide what is missing and run it again), 4 conflict, denied or invalid.
The stream is untouched unless the exit code is 0. Examples:
  ag integrate prop_8f3a1c                        any unique id prefix works
  ag integrate prop_8f3a1c --fencing-token 7      present the token of your exclusive lease
  ag --json integrate prop_8f3a1c                 stable blocker codes for scripts and agents
```

```text
Print an example policy document

Usage: ag policy example [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>     Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --as <IDENTITY>  Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --json           Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>   Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet          Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose        Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

```text
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

## ag policy preset show

```text
Print the policy document a preset makes, and what it means

Usage: ag policy preset show [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  solo, team, agents or strict

Options:
      --admin <IDENTITY>       Identity pattern allowed to change the policy (repeatable). Default: you
  -C, --repo <DIR>             Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --as <IDENTITY>          Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --issuer <IDENTITY=KEY>  Trust this CI issuer to sign the `tests` check: IDENTITY=PUBLIC_KEY, e.g. service:ci=<64 hex digits>
      --ci-key <NAME>          Trust the signing key NAME of this repository (created if missing; `ag validate keygen NAME` makes the same key): the issuer becomes service:NAME
      --json                   Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>           Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet                  Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose                Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
```

## ag policy preset apply

```text
Store a preset as the stream's next policy version (needs an admin)

Usage: ag policy preset apply [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  solo, team, agents or strict

Options:
      --admin <IDENTITY>       Identity pattern allowed to change the policy (repeatable). Default: you
  -C, --repo <DIR>             Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --as <IDENTITY>          Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --issuer <IDENTITY=KEY>  Trust this CI issuer to sign the `tests` check: IDENTITY=PUBLIC_KEY, e.g. service:ci=<64 hex digits>
      --ci-key <NAME>          Trust the signing key NAME of this repository (created if missing; `ag validate keygen NAME` makes the same key): the issuer becomes service:NAME
      --json                   Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>           Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
      --stream <STREAM>        Stream (default: the default stream)
  -q, --quiet                  Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose                Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
```

## ag policy explain

```text
Say in plain language what a policy allows, requires and refuses

Usage: ag policy explain [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]  A policy file, or `current` (the default) for the policy in force

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>       Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --stream <STREAM>  Stream whose policy `current` means (default: the default stream)
      --as <IDENTITY>    Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --json             Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>     Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet            Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose          Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version

Examples:
  ag policy explain                  the policy in force
  ag policy explain policy.json      a document, before you set it
  ag --json policy explain current   the same sentences as data
```

```text
  -v, --verbose        Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

## ag validate run

```text
Check out the exact candidate tree of a proposal, run a command on it and record a signed attestation of the result.

WARNING: the command runs on this machine without a sandbox. This runner is for trusted code and local workflows; use an isolated execution plane for untrusted code.

Usage: ag validate run [OPTIONS] --check <CHECK> --key <KEY> <PROPOSAL> -- <COMMAND>...

Arguments:
  <PROPOSAL>
          Proposal id

  <COMMAND>...
          The command and its arguments

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>
          Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)

      --check <CHECK>
          Check name, as listed in the policy's `required_validations`

      --as <IDENTITY>
          Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY

      --key <KEY>
          Name of the issuer key created with `ag validate keygen`

      --issuer <ISSUER>
          Issuer identity (default: `service:<key name>`)

      --json
          Machine-readable JSON output

      --color <WHEN>
          Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never

      --env <ENV>
          Environment digest to record (default: derived from the command and platform)

  -q, --quiet
          Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown

  -v, --verbose
          Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## ag agent

```text
Agent identities and runs

Usage: ag agent [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  register   Register an agent and create its signing key
  list       List agents
  start      Start a run. Prints the identity the agent must use (`agent:name#run_…`)
  finish     Finish a run and release its leases
  heartbeat  Heartbeat a running run
  runs       List runs, newest first
  reap       Abandon runs with no recent heartbeat and release their leases
  disable    Stop an agent from starting new runs
  enable     Allow a disabled agent to run again

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>     Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --as <IDENTITY>  Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --json           Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>   Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet          Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose        Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

## ag agent reap

```text
Abandon runs with no recent heartbeat and release their leases

Usage: ag agent reap [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>         Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Heartbeat timeout (default 10m here; with `--remote`, the server's `agents.run_stale_after_secs`)
      --as <IDENTITY>      Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --dry-run            Say what would be abandoned without changing anything
      --json               Machine-readable JSON output
      --remote [<NAME>]    Reap the runs of a server instead of this repository (needs `agent.operate` there; without a NAME: origin). The server also revokes the credentials bound to the reaped runs
      --color <WHEN>       Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet              Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose            Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

## ag task

```text
Tasks and their dependencies

Usage: ag task [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create    Create a task
  edit      Refine instructions before a task's first run; concurrent edits are refused
  attempts  Inspect or change a task's durable execution-attempt limit
  list      List tasks
  depend    Declare that TASK cannot start until ON is done
  ready     Open tasks whose dependencies are all done
  done      Mark a task done
  cancel    Cancel a task

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>     Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --as <IDENTITY>  Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --json           Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>   Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet          Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose        Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

## ag task create

```text
Create a task

Usage: ag task create [OPTIONS] <TITLE>

Arguments:
  <TITLE>  Title

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>                   Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
  -d, --description <DESCRIPTION>    Description [default: ""]
      --as <IDENTITY>                Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --scope <SCOPE>                Path glob the task is expected to touch (repeatable)
      --json                         Machine-readable JSON output
      --source-task <SOURCE_TASK>    Original task for an independent follow-up
      --color <WHEN>                 Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
      --source-run <SOURCE_RUN>      Failed or abandoned run of --source-task
      --max-attempts <MAX_ATTEMPTS>  Total runs permitted (0 leaves the server limit unset) [default: 0]
  -q, --quiet                        Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose                      Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                         Print help
  -V, --version                      Print version
```

## ag task edit

```text
Refine instructions before a task's first run; concurrent edits are refused

Usage: ag task edit [OPTIONS] <--title <TITLE>|--description <DESCRIPTION>|--scope <SCOPE>|--clear-scope> <TASK>

Arguments:
  <TASK>  Task identifier

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>                 Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --title <TITLE>              New title; omitted keeps the current title
      --as <IDENTITY>              Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --description <DESCRIPTION>  New description; an empty string clears it
      --json                       Machine-readable JSON output
      --scope <SCOPE>              Replace path scope (repeatable)
      --clear-scope                Remove the expected file-path scope (repository policy still applies)
      --color <WHEN>               Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet                      Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
      --remote [<NAME>]            Edit on a configured server instead of locally (default name: origin)
  -v, --verbose                    Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version
```

## ag remote

```text
Manage remotes and work with proposals, events and policy on a server

Usage: ag remote [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add         Add a remote
  list        List remotes
  remove      Forget a remote
  whoami      Show who the server thinks you are
  proposals   List proposals on the server
  proposal    Show a proposal with its reviews
  prepare     What would integrating do now, and what is missing?
  explain     Explain why a server proposal cannot land, with the next commands. Changes nothing
  reviewers   Inspect, add or remove requested reviewers (no approval or access change)
  review      Review a proposal's current head
  discussion  Read and participate in revision-bound line discussions
  integrate   Integrate a proposal into its stream
  close       Close a proposal without integrating it
  streams     List streams
  events      Show the events of the repository (replay), or follow them live
  policy      Show or set a stream's policy
  log         Show history of a revision on the server
  blame       Show which changeset introduced each line of a file on the server: `ag remote blame main:src/lib.rs`
  cat         Print a file as of a revision on the server: `ag remote cat main:src/lib.rs`

Options:
```

## ag login

```text
Save a server credential once; `clone`, `fetch`, `push` and `remote` then need no token plumbing

Usage: ag login [OPTIONS] <SERVER>

Arguments:
  <SERVER>  The server, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (a repository URL works too; only the server part is used)

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>         Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --token-stdin        Read the credential from standard input (`echo "$TOKEN" | ag login URL --token-stdin`)
      --as <IDENTITY>      Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --token-file <FILE>  Read the credential from a file (`ag-server dev` writes one and prints the command)
      --ca-file <CA_FILE>  Extra CA certificate (PEM) to trust when checking the credential
      --json               Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>       Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet              Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose            Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version

The credential is stored in credentials.json beside the user configuration (`ag config path`), readable by you only.
An environment variable (AG_TOKEN) or a credential stored with a remote still takes precedence. Examples:
  ag login http://127.0.0.1:8080 --token-file ag-dev-data/dev/token
  echo "$TOKEN" | ag login https://ag.example.com --token-stdin
```

## ag auth status

```text
List saved connections; --check asks each server whether its saved credential still works

Usage: ag auth status [OPTIONS] [SERVER]

Arguments:
  [SERVER]  Inspect just this server (a repository URL works too)

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>         Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --check              Verify saved credentials online. Without this, status is local and works offline
      --as <IDENTITY>      Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Timeout for each online check, in seconds [default: 5]
      --ca-file <CA_FILE>  Extra CA certificate (PEM) for online checks
      --json               Machine-readable JSON output
      --color <WHEN>       Colour the output: auto (a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set), always or never
  -q, --quiet              Print only what was asked for: no confirmations or hints. Errors and refusals are still shown
  -v, --verbose            Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

## ag config

```text

Commands:
  list   Show every setting with its effective value and where it comes from
  get    Print one setting's effective value (see `list` for the keys)
  set    Store a user-level setting: `identity` or `color`
  unset  Remove a stored user-level setting
  path   Print the locations of the configuration files

Options:
  -C, --repo <DIR>     Operate on the repository at this path (default: discovered from the current directory)
      --as <IDENTITY>  Act as this identity (`user:alice`, `agent:bot#run_…`, `service:ci`). Also: AG_IDENTITY

  -v, --verbose        Explain what is happening on standard error: repository, identity, remote, timing
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version

Files, environment variables and precedence: ag help config
```
